# blitz-2010-fn103-and-pinpoints
- **URL:** https://scholarship.law.okcu.edu/downloads/d7kcg-2ck33/fulltext.pdf · **Accessed:** 2026-09-16 · **For:** v2 review, Phase 1 slice B
- **What it establishes:** Page pinpoints in Blitz, 2010 Wis. L. Rev. 1049 (PDF text-extracted; HeinOnline running feet give the WLR pages). "Functional equivalent of thought" formulation at 1072; Part heading "B. Functional Equivalents of Thought" at 1073; Otto's journal → brain chip at 1067; "journal or iPhone" at 1073; chip "left outside of one's skull (say, in a cap)" at 1073–74; footnote 103 (Baumgartner) on 1069. No surveillance/observation/reading argument anywhere: "surveil" absent; "Fourth Amendment" only in citations and one forced-medication passage (~1097).
- **Key passages:** "freedom of thought cannot and should not protect all activity that arises from or influences thought, but rather activity that is either (1) the functional equivalent of thought, or (2) a reshaping of the self that does that thinking" (1072) · fn. 103: "See, e.g., Baumgartner v. United States, 322 U.S. 665, 673-74, 676-77 (1944) (rejecting an attempt to use a person's allegedly pro-Nazi private diary entries as a basis for revoking citizenship and emphasizing that one of the prerogatives of citizenship is 'the freedom to speak foolishly and without moderation')" (1069) · "the protagonist's opening rebellion against thought control begins with an entry in a diary" (1069).
- **Reliability:** Primary scholarly source (repository PDF of the published article); independent.
- **Relevance to this project:** III9 (l.74); ref [29] pinpoints; supports "a liberty to use" and "Blitz did not argue" the observation liberty.
